name: Live sports betting risk & odds management
category: New — sportsbook ops, in-play wager risk
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Live (in-play) sports betting risk and odds management — per-(player, market) wager velocity, per-account exposure counters, per-market sharp-money detection (high-volume wagers from CLV-positive accounts), per-event book exposure / liability features, plus stake-factoring / player-profiling, responsible-gambling velocity intervention, AML transaction monitoring, and integrity / match-fixing bet-pattern features at sub-second update cadence for in-play and micro-betting (pitch-by-pitch, drive-by-drive, point-by-point) markets.
domain_fit.one_line_definition: An in-play sportsbook trading / risk engine decides on every wager-placement, score-update, line-move and account-action event — typically inside 50–500 ms — whether to accept, reprice, stake-factor, suspend, hold, or flag (CLV-sharp, AML, integrity, responsible-gambling) the bet, based on rolling per-(player, market) wager velocity, per-account exposure, per-market sharp-money concentration, and per-event book liability counters.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Real-time per-event / per-market liability and exposure management — maintain a rolling counter of stake_accepted, max_payout_on_each_outcome, net_position and worst-case-loss per (event_id, market_id, selection_id) so traders and the odds engine can hedge, move lines, or suspend markets before exposure breaches the configured liability cap (Kambi, Genius Sports, OddsMatrix all describe this as the core trader-facing surface). 2) Sharp-money / CLV-positive account detection — per-account rolling CLV (price taken vs closing price), per-account hit-rate vs implied probability, per-account beat-the-close streak, per-(account, sport, market_type) profitability — feed automated stake-factoring (cut stake to 50 % → 25 % → 10 % → 1 % of max as profitability climbs); per-(market, time_bucket) coordinated-sharp inflow ('steam') detection across multiple sharp accounts moving the same side within a 60–300 s window. 3) Per-(player, market) wager velocity for responsible-gambling and AML — rolling stakes_24h, deposits_24h, time-on-app, bets_per_minute, n_unique markets_60min, deposit-without-play ratios; trigger cool-off, mandatory deposit-limit prompts, or AML SAR review when state-mandated thresholds (CO, MA, NJ, NC) trip. 4) In-play micro-market pricing inputs — Simplebet / DraftKings-style pitch-by-pitch markets need rolling per-(pitcher, batter) and per-(player, situation) features (last-N-pitch outcome distribution, current-drive yards-per-play velocity, last-quarter pace) updated within a single play-clock tick. 5) Pre-bet bet-validation gating — per-account count(active_bets_on_same_event), count(SGP_with_correlation_high), count(distinct_devices_24h), count(failed_geocomply_checks) for collusion, bonus-abuse and self-exclusion enforcement. 6) Integrity / match-fixing inputs — per-(event, market) anomalous-stake concentration, n_unique accounts wagering on the longshot in the last N minutes, per-(account, league) hit-rate divergence — fed into Sportradar UFDS / IBIA Integrity Exchange / Genius Sports Bet Monitoring. 7) Multi-account / collusion detection — per-(device_fp, ip_hash, payment_method) n_unique account_ids, per-(account, account) co-betting overlap for bonus-abuse and arbitrage rings.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events landing in beava as @bv.event: wager_placed {ts, bet_id, account_id, event_id, market_id, selection_id, sport, league, price_taken_decimal, stake, currency, leg_count, sgp_bool, device_fp, ip_hash, geo_state, channel(web|ios|android|retail)}; wager_resolved {ts, bet_id, account_id, event_id, outcome(win|loss|push|void), payout, closing_price_decimal}; price_update {ts, event_id, market_id, selection_id, new_price_decimal, source(trader|model|feed)}; market_state_change {ts, event_id, market_id, state(open|suspended|settled|cancelled)}; deposit {ts, account_id, amount, method(card|ach|paypal|skrill|crypto)}; withdrawal {ts, account_id, amount, method}; login {ts, account_id, device_fp, ip_hash, geo_state, kyc_status}; rg_action {ts, account_id, action(deposit_limit_set|cool_off|self_exclude), value}; score_event {ts, event_id, score_home, score_away, clock_seconds, period, last_play_id}; cashout_offered {ts, bet_id, cashout_price, accepted_bool}; geocomply_check {ts, account_id, geo_state, result(pass|fail|spoof_suspect)}. Highest-rate streams are price_update (driven by ~1M odds/sec from data feeds like Sportradar, Genius, TxODDS, OpticOdds), score_event (per-pitch / per-play tick), and wager_placed during peak in-play moments (Super Bowl peaks reached ~15k tx/s at GeoComply in 2025).
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy reuse of beava counter / velocity / distance / distribution / n_unique primitives over sliding windows (last 60 s, last 5 min, last 1 h, last 24 h, last 7 d, lifetime-of-event, lifetime-of-account). Per-(event_id, market_id, selection_id): sum(stake), sum(potential_payout), net_position = sum(stake) - sum(potential_payout_if_wins), count(wager), velocity(stake_per_min), distribution(price_taken) for adverse-selection, n_unique(account_id) — the canonical trader liability surface. Per-account: count(wager, 1h/24h/7d), sum(stake, ...), sum(net_pnl), velocity(stake_per_hour), distribution(price_taken_vs_close) (the CLV histogram), rolling z-score(roi_vs_sport_baseline), count(beat_close, last_50), n_unique(market_type, 24h) (specialization signal), distance(geo_state_t, geo_state_t-1) for VPN / multi-account; count(active_bets_on_event), count(failed_geocomply, 24h). Per-(account, sport, market_type): count(wager), sum(net_pnl), CLV running mean — the canonical stake-factoring input. Per-(market_id, 60s/300s window): count(wager), sum(stake_on_each_selection), velocity(stake_per_min_by_side), n_unique(account_id_by_side), n_unique(sharp_account_id_by_side) — the canonical steam / sharp-inflow detector. Per-(device_fp): n_unique(account_id, 7d), count(login, 24h). Per-(ip_hash): n_unique(account_id, 24h). Per-(payment_method_hash): n_unique(account_id) for fraud rings. Per-(pitcher, batter), per-(player, situation) rolling distributions for micro-market pricing.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and high-cardinality. Primary keys: account_id, bet_id, (event_id, market_id, selection_id), event_id, market_id, device_fp, ip_hash, payment_method_hash, plus ordered pairs / triples (account_id, sport), (account_id, market_type), (account_id, event_id), (account_id, device_fp), (event_id, market_id, side), (pitcher_id, batter_id) for MLB pitch-level, (player_id, situation_code) for NFL/NBA player-prop micro-markets. Liability and steam features are keyed on the (event, market, selection) triple; account-profiling features are keyed on account_id alone; sharp-inflow / coordinated-action features are keyed on (market_id, time_bucket).
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: All families show up. Tumbling per-event (a fixture is the natural session — most liability resets on settlement). Sliding for sharp-inflow / steam (60 s, 300 s), per-account velocity (1h, 24h, 7d), and CLV running average. Session windows align with login / app-foreground sessions for responsible-gambling time-on-app metrics. Approximate aggregates are mostly acceptable: HLL for n_unique(account_id) per (market, time_bucket), CMS for top-K accounts staking on a suspect market, T-Digest for the CLV / price-taken distribution, Bloom for known-sharp / self-excluded membership. STRICT-EXACT counters are required for liability (sum(stake) and sum(potential_payout) must be exact — money is on the line) and for AML reporting thresholds (CTR / SAR triggers cannot tolerate approximation under FinCEN / FATF / 5AMLD).
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Mixed but with strict zones. Per-bet liability accumulation must be strictly no-double-count and idempotent on bet_id — duplicate-counting a $10k wager into the liability counter could cause a wrongly-suspended market or, worse, a wrongly-accepted offsetting bet. Per-account stake_24h for AML / responsible-gambling triggers must also be strict (CTR threshold is $10k cash equivalent, RG limits are state-mandated). Sharp-money / CLV / steam / micro-market features can tolerate at-least-once with idempotent keys (event_id + selection_id + ts_bucket) — a duplicate-counted wager biases the steam signal mildly toward 'flag', which is safe. Bet acceptance itself is exactly-once on bet_id at the wager service (transactionally-safe path), and beava's role is feature aggregation feeding that path.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Three operating points. (a) Bet-acceptance / pre-trade gating path: p99 < 50 ms feature batch_get is the workable budget; sportsbooks already run a 3–8 second bet-delay spool for material-event protection, but the per-feature read inside that spool is on the critical path. (b) In-play odds / micro-market reprice path: p99 < 200 ms because end-to-end odds-feed latency (TxODDS Tx Fusion advertises 8–10 ms, the competitive benchmark is sub-200 ms) caps the budget; market suspension is the failure mode if features lag. (c) Trader-dashboard / post-bet exposure refresh and async risk-scoring: 500 ms – 2 s is fine. Beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits all three with headroom; per-decision feature fan-out is 20–60 features on the pre-trade path and 60–150 on the model-scoring path (sharp-detection ensembles, RG ML scorers).
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second on the in-play / micro-market path (an unrepriced market on a goal / red-zone snap / break point is the exact 'getting picked off' failure mode Kambi and Bayes Esports describe and Genius Sports' BetVision is designed to close). Sub-100 ms is the de-facto target for the highest-tier in-play products (Simplebet pitch-by-pitch, BetVision). Single-digit-second freshness is acceptable for the AML / stake-factoring / responsible-gambling triggers (state intervention rules are minute-scale, not sub-second). Beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop is materially fresher than the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pattern bet365, FanDuel and Sportradar describe in their public architectures. [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly operator-dependent and extremely peaky. Steady-state for a top-3 US operator (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM) is plausibly 10k–50k EPS aggregated across wager + price-update + score + login + geocomply (DraftKings handles ~$2B+ in Super Bowl handle through Aerospike clusters expanding from 6–10 to 16–20 nodes at peak). Super Bowl 2025: GeoComply alone recorded ~15k transactions/sec pre-kickoff, and FanDuel handled 16.6M bets that Sunday — implying sustained 100k+ EPS aggregated across the live-betting subsystem during the second-half micro-market window. Odds-feed input alone is published as ~1M odds/sec (OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, TxODDS). A regional operator or B2B trading platform (OddsMatrix processes 1.5M bets/day = ~17 EPS sustained, ~hundreds at peak) easily fits one beava node. AAA US operator at Super Bowl / March Madness scale requires partitioning beyond single-node beava (a single Apple-M4 core at ~684k EPS covers the wager+score streams but not the full odds-feed firehose). Bayes Esports describes spikes 5× average on tournament days. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 3:1 to 10:1 reads-per-write on the pre-trade path (every wager_placed triggers one write and 20–60 batch_get features for risk / RG / sharp / liability gating). Heavier read-skew (20:1+) on the trader dashboard and the odds-engine reprice loop (same (event, market, selection) liability features re-fetched many times per second per market). Overall read-leaning, similar to recsys ranking and unlike pure ad-tech telemetry.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by account_id, event_id × market_id × selection_id, and bet_id cardinality. Mid-sized US operator (~5M active accounts, ~50k live events/year × ~200 markets × ~3 selections ≈ 30M market-selection rows live, ~50M bets/month): ~5M accounts × ~150 counter slots × ~32 B ≈ 24 GB; ~30M live (event, market, selection) × ~30 slots × 32 B ≈ 29 GB; per-(market, time_bucket) sharp counters at ~30M × ~10 slots × 32 B ≈ 10 GB; device / ip / payment dedup ~10–50 GB. Total 75–150 GB hot state, comfortably in RAM on a 256–512 GB box. Top-3 US operator at Super Bowl scale (DraftKings, FanDuel) exceeds single-node beava and needs partitioning. Smaller B2B trading vendors (GAN, OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, Kambi Tzeract) per-tenant fits cleanly on a single node. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on account_id (US handle grew ~22.8 % YoY 2025, account base grows similarly), explosive on bet_id (millions/day at AAA scale, but bet-level features are usually per-account aggregates and bet_id state TTLs immediately on settlement), explosive on (event_id, market_id, selection_id) on micro-betting / SGP / player-prop platforms (a single NFL game now spawns hundreds of player-prop + micro-markets — Simplebet, DraftKings, FanDuel publicly cite 50–200+ markets per major game), bounded on sport / market_type / state / channel. Device_fp and ip_hash are explosive; HLL n_unique is the right primitive. Match_id (sports event) is bounded for the season but per-market multiplication is the dominant growth axis.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Highly variable by primitive. Liability per (event, market, selection): lifetime of the event (minutes for pitch-level micro-markets, hours for an in-play NFL game, multi-day for tournaments — Bayes Esports cites 10k live matches/yr per platform). Per-account rolling features: 7–30 days sliding for stake-factoring / CLV; lifetime-of-account for player-profile baselines. AML transaction-monitoring features: 30–90 days minimum for SAR analysis, with UK Gambling Commission requiring at least 5 years retention of underlying records (William Hill cites 7 years) — the live counter lives in beava but the raw record archives to a warehouse. Per-(market, 300s) sharp / steam buckets: minutes. Per-(device_fp, ip_hash) for collusion: 30–90 days.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20–60 features per pre-trade bet-acceptance decision (per-account velocity, per-account CLV / stake-factor, per-event liability, per-market sharp inflow, per-account RG state, per-account AML state, per-device fanout). 60–150 features on the ML scoring path (sharp / collusion ensembles, RG ML scorers like Bettor Sense, anomaly detection). Strongly favours the batch_get path beava ships.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Crash-safe is the baseline; regulator-grade is required for the AML / liability slice. Liability counters that drift across a crash could cause direct financial loss (mispriced markets, missed hedges) — beava's WAL + snapshot is the right shape, but the bet record itself is the source of truth in the transactional wager database (PostgreSQL / Oracle at most operators). AML transaction-monitoring records, SAR filings, geocomply audit trails and RG intervention records must be retained for 5–7 years in a regulator-grade store (S3 / Iceberg / lakehouse + immutable audit log) — beava is in-memory and refuses network FS, so beava's role is the live online feature, not the archive. Internal-controls / SOC1 / SOC2 audits at public operators (DraftKings, Flutter, Entain, Penn, Caesars are all SEC-registered) require explainable risk decisions, which favours beava's deterministic primitives over Flink SQL black-boxes.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for single-binary regional / sidecar deployments alongside the wager-acceptance service and the odds engine — exactly the pattern DraftKings describes for its Aerospike low-latency coordination layer, and what FanDuel achieves via AWS Local Zones / Wavelength / Outposts to satisfy per-state regulatory geo-isolation. Sportsbook architectures are already per-state (US PASPA-post regulation requires per-jurisdiction stack) and per-region (UK Gambling Commission, MGA, AGCO Ontario, all major EU regulators), which maps directly to beava's single-binary regional-node story. Hard ceilings: beava v0 has no in-process sharding (a top-3 US operator at Super Bowl needs to hand-shard externally), no native multi-tenancy (B2B vendors like Kambi, GAN, OddsMatrix serving many operators on one box have no isolation primitives), no triggers (sportsbooks fundamentally want 'suspend market when liability_z > N' and 'stake-factor when CLV streak > M'), refuse-on-network-FS forces local-NVMe WAL planning.

commercial_fit.who_buys: (a) Sportsbook trading and risk teams inside tier-1 B2C operators (DraftKings, FanDuel/Flutter, BetMGM/Entain-MGM, Caesars/William Hill, bet365, Penn Entertainment/ESPN Bet, Hard Rock Bet, Fanatics Sportsbook, PointsBet, Rush Street Interactive/BetRivers/SugarHouse, Bally Bet, Underdog, PrizePicks, Sleeper). (b) B2B sportsbook platform / trading vendors who would embed beava rather than buy a Redis cluster — Kambi (Tzeract), Genius Sports (BetVision, Trading Services), Sportradar (Managed Trading Services, ad:s, Insight Tech Services), OddsMatrix (EveryMatrix), OpticOdds (Copilot), GAN, GR8 Tech, Altenar, BtoBet, Digitain, FSB Technology, Bayes Esports, IMG Arena, Stats Perform, TxODDS, LSports, BetGenius. (c) Integrity / regulatory vendors — Sportradar Integrity Services (UFDS), IBIA Integrity Exchange, US Integrity, ESIC (esports), GLI / iGB compliance. (d) Anti-fraud / RG vendors integrating with sportsbooks — GeoComply, Mindway AI BetBuddy, Optimove, Bettor Sense, Featurespace ARIC for AML, ComplyAdvantage, Sumsub, Jumio. (e) State lottery operators that have launched mobile sportsbook (DC Lottery / Intralot, Oregon Lottery, NH Lottery / DraftKings, Washington DC, Rhode Island / IGT). Buyer persona: Trading Director / Head of Risk / Director of Sportsbook Operations / Head of Integrity / Head of Responsible Gambling / Head of AML — distinct from corporate fraud and growth, sometimes embedded in a single 'Sportsbook Operations' org.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and growth-stage. (1) Global online sports betting market: Grand View Research USD 100.9B (2024) -> USD 187.39B (2030) at ~11 % CAGR; ResearchAndMarkets USD 155.4B (2025) -> USD 256.5B (2030) at 10.54 %; methodology variance reflects whether handle, GGR or operator revenue is the unit. (2) US regulated sports betting: USD 16.96B GGR in 2025 on USD 166.94B handle (+22.8 % YoY) across 39 states + DC + PR; New Jersey alone USD 13.96B handle / USD 1.18B GGR in 2025; US national hold avg 10.15 %. (3) AGA estimated USD 1.7B handle for Super Bowl 60 (Feb 2026) and USD 3.3B for March Madness — single events generating tens of millions of bet events. (4) FanDuel handled 16.6M bets on Super Bowl Sunday 2025 (Flutter Q4 2025 release). (5) B2B trading / platform vendor revenue: Kambi public revenue ~EUR 175M+ (2024 trailing), Sportradar 2024 revenue ~EUR 1.1B, Genius Sports 2024 revenue ~USD 511M, Bayes Esports raised funding from Sportradar, OddsMatrix part of EveryMatrix (>EUR 250M revenue). (6) Integrity spend: Sportradar UFDS monitors ~850k events/yr across 70 sports, identifies ~1,329 suspicious matches in 2023. The 'risk engine + odds engine + integrity + RG / AML' substrate is consistently a 5–15 % infrastructure spend line at tier-1 operators. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Live / in-play share is now >50 % of handle at most operators and >70 % in esports (Bayes Esports / PandaScore data) — the entire industry tailwind is shifting to the surface beava is best at, while legacy Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipelines hit latency walls. 2) Micro-betting explosion (DraftKings acquired Simplebet in 2024, FanDuel rolled SGP correlation engine, Genius Sports launched BetVision computer-vision in-play markets) — 10–100× the per-game market count means 10–100× the per-event state, which legacy systems struggle to keep hot. 3) Player-prop integrity scandals (MLB Emmanuel Clase / Luis L. Ortiz 2025; NBA Jontay Porter 2024; NCAA prop-bet bans in IL, OH, MD, VT) — regulators are imposing real-time integrity-monitoring obligations, IBIA + Sportradar UFDS adoption accelerating. 4) Responsible-gambling regulation tightening — CO, MA, NJ, NC mandating algorithmic RG intervention (2024–2025); UK Gambling Commission affordability checks (Apr 2025); Australia BetStop national self-exclusion; Ontario AGCO problem-gambling KPIs. 5) AML pressure — FinCEN advisories on sports-betting laundering (2024), BSA expansion to crypto-payment sportsbooks, FATF gambling guidance (2024), 6AMLD in EU. 6) Sharp / arbitrage / bonus-abuse losses pushing operators to faster stake-factoring (Smart Betting Club / Profiling Tips both document the 50 % → 25 % → 10 % → 1 % cascade). 7) Competitive latency arms race — TxODDS Tx Fusion 8–10 ms odds, sub-200 ms competitive benchmark, bet365 Diffusion architecture. 8) Prediction-market disruption (Kalshi, Polymarket sports markets 2025) is forcing regulated sportsbooks to compete on UX speed and pricing accuracy.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: Heavy and jurisdiction-fragmented. US: state-by-state regulators (NJ DGE, NV GCB, NY NYSGC, IL IGB, PA PGCB, MI MGCB, CO DOG, MA MGC, NC NCSLGC, etc.) with bespoke real-time-reporting feeds, FinCEN BSA (CTR > USD 10k, SAR), state AML and integrity-monitoring rules, GeoComply-mandated geo-fencing, IRS W-2G winnings reporting; states with algorithmic RG mandates (CO, MA, NJ, NC). UK: Gambling Commission LCCP, 5+ year record retention, affordability checks 2025, mandatory integrity-monitoring reporting to GC and IBIA. EU: 5AMLD/6AMLD AML obligations on gambling operators, GDPR Art. 17 right-to-erasure tension with retention, MGA (Malta), AAMS/ADM (Italy), DGOJ (Spain), ARJEL (France), regional regulators. Other: Ontario AGCO, Australia ACMA, MGA-like rules. Cross-cutting: PCI-DSS for payments, SOC2 for SaaS exposure, IGT-style change-management for any code touching market settlement. EU AI Act (2026) — automated stake-factoring decisions affecting access to service may be high-risk AI requiring explainability. EU DSA may apply to large operator platforms over 45M MAU thresholds. The combination of strict liability-counter exactness + 5–7 year retention + sub-second latency is the unusual constraint stack that beava maps to (live in RAM + WAL + archive-to-lakehouse).
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast for the demo, slow for production. 1–3 days to a credible per-account stake_24h + per-(event, market, selection) liability sum + per-(market, 5min) steam-detection + per-account CLV demo on beava with simulated NFL / NBA / MLB events; the @bv.event / @bv.table model maps cleanly to wager_placed / wager_resolved / price_update. A realistic 40–80-feature pilot at a tier-2 operator or a B2B trading vendor is 6–12 weeks once auth, TLS and per-tenant namespaces are added (the v0 gaps below). A tier-1 US operator (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM) procurement cycle is 6–18 months because of regulator change-control and SEC-level audit chain.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack: Redis + Lua (counters + windows + Bloom/CMS/TopK modules) is the de-facto bet-acceptance feature cache at virtually every operator (FanDuel uses Redis aggressively per Tinybird / Optimove case studies; DraftKings uses Aerospike as a low-latency layer alongside Redis). Aerospike is the high-profile choice for the lowest-latency bet-acceptance path (DraftKings public case study; SSD-optimised). Apache Kafka + Apache Flink (or Spark Structured Streaming, RisingWave, Materialize) is the streaming backbone — FanDuel publicly uses Confluent + Flink; bet365 publicly uses Diffusion (Push Technology) for client-fanout; Ververica/Decodable highlight sports betting as a Flink reference vertical. Hazelcast for in-memory grid use cases. ClickHouse / Pinot / Druid for the trader-dashboard OLAP path. Tinybird for serving real-time APIs (FanDuel customer). PostgreSQL / Oracle for the wager system-of-record. Snowflake / Databricks / Redshift for the offline analytics path. Tecton / Hopsworks / Feast as managed online feature stores feeding ML scorers — but rarely adopted in sportsbook trading because the latency budget is tighter than typical ML inference.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: B2B sportsbook platform + trading vendors (most direct competitive context for beava as a substrate): Kambi (Turnkey Sportsbook + Tzeract AI trading), Sportradar (Managed Trading Services, ad:s, Insight Tech Services, UFDS Integrity), Genius Sports (Trading Services + BetVision computer-vision in-play), OddsMatrix (EveryMatrix), OpticOdds (Copilot sportsbook management), GR8 Tech, Altenar, BtoBet (Aspire Global / NeoGames), Digitain, FSB Technology, Pronet Gaming, BetConstruct, SBTech (acquired by DraftKings 2020), IMG Arena, Stats Perform, TxODDS, LSports, BetGenius. Micro-betting + ML pricing: Simplebet (acquired by DraftKings 2024), Huddle, Metric Gaming, Quants AI. Integrity-specific: Sportradar Integrity Services, US Integrity, IBIA Integrity Exchange, ESIC. Responsible-gambling-specific: Mindway AI BetBuddy, Bettor Sense, Optimove, Featurespace (now Visa). AML / KYC / geo-compliance: GeoComply, Sumsub, ComplyAdvantage, Featurespace ARIC, Trustly, Jumio. Beava would naturally sit underneath (as a feature substrate) any of the B2B trading platforms or as a sidecar inside an operator's in-house risk engine — not replace the trading workflow or the integrity-monitoring vendor.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the per-state / per-jurisdiction regulated topology that US sportsbooks are forced into (FanDuel uses AWS Local Zones + Wavelength + Outposts; per-state stacks are the default). 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / liability / distribution / distance features sportsbook risk literally lives on, including beava's distance primitive directly expressing impossible-travel for VPN / multi-account detection and price-vs-close distance for CLV — without writing Flink SQL, Redis Lua or hand-rolled Aerospike UDFs. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits the bet-acceptance latency budget (well inside DraftKings-class Aerospike latency, beats Kafka -> Flink -> materialized view pipelines). 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core — attractive to mid-tier operators (Penn/ESPN Bet, Hard Rock Bet, Fanatics, Rush Street, PointsBet, Underdog, PrizePicks, Sleeper, every state lottery sportsbook) and especially to B2B vendors (Altenar, BtoBet, GR8 Tech, FSB, Digitain) who cannot or will not depend on Redis Source Available licence drift or a managed-cloud feature store. 5) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how wager-acceptance gateways and odds feeds already shape events (TxODDS / Sportradar feeds, in-house wager-acceptance microservices). 6) Native composite-key aggregations — (event_id, market_id, selection_id), (account_id, sport, market_type), (market_id, time_bucket), (device_fp, ip_hash) are first-class in @bv.table; Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes and Aerospike requires UDF work. 7) Deterministic, explainable primitives — auditor / SEC-disclosure / SOC2 / state-regulator friendly, in contrast to Flink SQL pipelines whose recovery semantics auditors struggle to certify. 8) Refuse-on-network-FS bias maps well to the local-NVMe-WAL pattern that DraftKings-class operators already deploy.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment in a regulated sportsbook (state-licence conditions, SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR all require authenticated access); effectively limits beava to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. 2) No in-process sharding — tier-1 US operators (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM) at Super Bowl / March Madness scale exceed single-node beava; tier-1 B2B trading platforms (Kambi, Sportradar Managed Trading) need horizontal partition by tenant. 3) No triggers / 'fire when (event_id, market_id, selection_id).net_position crosses liability_cap, suspend market' — this is the single most-cited workflow gap for the trading-engine path; sportsbook trading is fundamentally event-driven (suspend, reprice, hedge, stake-factor, alert) and polling 30+ features per wager wastes round-trips on the critical path. 4) In-memory only — AML / SAR / integrity-monitoring records must be archived to a regulator-grade 5–7 year store; beava is not that archive and the integration pattern (WAL replay + Iceberg / Parquet sink) needs to be documented. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives — B2B trading vendors (Kambi, OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, Altenar, GR8 Tech) serving many operators on one substrate need per-tenant namespaces, quotas, per-tenant audit; beava v0 ships none. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list top-K (event, market) by liability_z over last 1 h' query — kills the trader-dashboard surface; trader-facing tools (Kambi, OddsMatrix) advertise this exact view as core. 7) Strict-exact monetary accumulation — the sum(stake) / sum(potential_payout) counter must be strictly idempotent on bet_id with zero loss under crash; beava's WAL + snapshot model needs explicit documentation and benchmarking that no double-count or loss is possible across crash + replay. 8) No native correlation engine for SGP / parlay leg correlation — OpticOdds SGP Engine and FanDuel's correlation models are the competition for that specific feature, and beava is a counter substrate not a correlation pricer (though it can feed one). 9) No native PII story for state-mandated retention windows (5+ years UK, varying US states), right-to-erasure under GDPR Art. 17 cascading through aggregates, IP / device-fp hashing at rest. 10) No published benchmark for the strict-monetary path with the read-load profile sportsbook traders generate (20:1 read:write on liability features); the 684k EPS number is push-only. 11) No integration with the published odds-feed protocols (Sportradar UOF, Genius LiveData, BetGenius Plug-in, TxODDS Fusion, IMG Arena, Stats Perform OPTA), all of which use bespoke binary or AMQP feeds. 12) No native graph / cohort primitives for multi-account / bonus-abuse / collusion ring detection (which Sportradar UFDS handles).
competition.integration_surface: Producers: wager-acceptance service (HTTP/JSON or TCP push from the wager gateway), odds engine (price_update events from the trading platform — Kambi, Genius, Sportradar, in-house), score feed (Sportradar UOF, Genius LiveData, OPTA, IMG Arena — typically via Kafka or AMQP bridge), payment processor (deposit / withdrawal events), KYC / geo-compliance (Sumsub, Jumio, GeoComply via webhook), responsible-gambling intervention service (RG_action events). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits in-house microservices and webhook producers; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput odds-feed gateways and wager-acceptance services. Consumers: trading platform reprice loop (Kambi, Sportradar MTS, in-house), bet-acceptance gating logic, trader dashboard (current generation: ClickHouse/Pinot — beava feeds them or co-exists), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM stake-factoring models, Bayesian sharp-detection ensembles, transformer-based anomaly detectors, RG scorers like Bettor Sense and Mindway BetBuddy), integrity-monitoring outbound feed to Sportradar UFDS / IBIA Integrity Exchange. Beava is the feature substrate underneath these, not a replacement for the odds feed or the trading platform.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Sportsbook risk decisions are split between deterministic rules (liability_cap, max-stake-per-market, state-mandated RG deposit limits, AML CTR/SAR thresholds, geo-fence, self-exclude — these are state-licence-driven and must be exact and auditable) and ML scorers (sharp / stake-factor models, RG ML scorers, collusion-graph detectors, dynamic-pricing models). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from both — same batch_get path feeds rules evaluation and ML scoring, which is its natural seam. Many operators run XGBoost / LightGBM for stake-factoring on top of beava-class features, and Bayesian / GBM ensembles for sharp detection.

adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum-adjacent. Sportsbook risk is one of the most adversarial domains in real-time systems — adversaries include professional sharps and syndicates (steam-move coordination across 3+ books in <60 s), arbitrage bots, courtsiders / latency-arbitrage exploiters, multi-account bonus-abuse rings, match-fixers (Sportradar UFDS flagged ~1,329 suspicious matches 2023), affiliated-betting collusion (Jontay Porter / Emmanuel Clase scandals 2024–2025), VPN / location-spoof bettors, money launderers using deposit-bet-cashout cycling. Pattern drift is fast (sharps move with line / market structure changes; new prop-bet markets create new arbitrage seams) but probably slightly slower than fraud / anti-cheat — comparable in iteration cadence to AML, faster than ad-tech IVT.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Acting as the wager system-of-record / general ledger — bet placement is a transactional database problem (PostgreSQL / Oracle / NewSQL) and money settlement must be ACID with full audit; beava is the live feature aggregator next to that database, not a replacement. 2) Acting as the odds engine / pricing model itself — that is Simplebet / Huddle / Kambi Tzeract / Sportradar trading / Genius Sports BetVision territory and involves simulation, computer-vision and model-serving infrastructure beava doesn't ship. 3) Long historical lookback for AML SAR investigation (5–7 year retention under UK GC, 5+ year FinCEN BSA) and integrity-monitoring forensics — that belongs in Parquet / Iceberg / Snowflake / Databricks, not in beava's in-memory state. 4) Cross-event / cross-account graph clustering for collusion / bonus-abuse rings (Sportradar UFDS, Featurespace ARIC) — beava has no join engine. 5) Full bet-history archive / KYC document store / GDPR audit log — beava is a live feature backend, not a system-of-record. 6) Settlement / resulting / void / push / cashout-price calculation — these are deterministic ledger operations off the bet record, not feature aggregates. 7) Acting as the rules engine, the trader dashboard, the integrity-monitoring submission to IBIA, or the regulator-facing real-time reporting feed (most states require structured XML/JSON reports to the licensing authority) — beava feeds these surfaces, not is them. 8) Multi-region active-active in v0 — sportsbook is per-state / per-jurisdiction by regulation so active-active is rarely demanded inside one regulated stack, but cross-jurisdiction operator aggregation requires it. 9) Computer-vision tracking of live events (Genius Sports BetVision, Stats Perform OPTA Tracking) — those produce events beava consumes, not the other way around. 10) Strict regulator-grade durability for the bet-record itself — beava could keep crash-safe live counters but the bet record is in a relational + warehouse store. 11) Player KYC / identity verification / age verification (Sumsub / Jumio / GeoComply territory).
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for sportsbook in-play risk, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the push and admin surfaces — without this, no regulated operator (state-licence, SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR exposure) can deploy externally; this is the single largest blocker for the domain. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (event_id, market_id, selection_id).net_position crosses liability_cap, suspend market' and 'when (account_id).clv_streak > N, drop stake_factor to next bracket' — sportsbook risk is fundamentally event-driven (suspend, reprice, stake-factor, hedge, RG-intervene, AML-flag) and polling 30+ features per wager wastes round-trips on the bet-acceptance hot path; documented as the single most-cited workflow gap. 3) Strict-exact monetary primitives with bet_id idempotency keys and crash-safe sum / count semantics — money is on the line, the WAL + snapshot model must be benchmarked and documented to prove no double-count and no loss across crash + replay (this is the gating audit / SOC1 question for any operator). 4) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, per-tenant rate-limit accounting and per-tenant audit logs for B2B trading vendors (Kambi, OddsMatrix, OpticOdds, Altenar, GR8 Tech) serving many operators on one substrate. 5) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix (account_id, event_id, market_id) so tier-1 operators (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM) at Super Bowl / March Madness scale stay within one cluster without external hand-sharding. 6) Per-key TTL and sliding-window eviction so explosive (event_id, market_id, selection_id) cardinality (millions/day at micro-market scale) doesn't OOM. 7) Secondary indexes / 'list top-K (event, market, selection) by liability_z over last 1 h' and 'top-K accounts by clv_30d' so trader dashboards and stake-factor reviews don't need to materialize the keyspace; this is core to Kambi / OddsMatrix / OpticOdds trader UX. 8) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives as first-class for n_unique(account, by_(market, 5min)), known-sharp Bloom membership, top-K liability events — surface them prominently in this domain's docs with worked examples. 9) Composite-key aggregations as first-class: (event_id, market_id, selection_id), (account_id, sport, market_type), (market_id, time_bucket), (device_fp, ip_hash) — ergonomic in @bv.table DSL. 10) Documented archive integration to Parquet / Iceberg / Snowflake / Databricks for AML SAR / integrity-monitoring / regulator audit (5–7 year retention) — beava lives next to a lakehouse, not on its own. 11) Native PII story: IP / device-fp hashing at rest, configurable per-namespace retention, right-to-erasure cascading (GDPR Art. 17), state-by-state retention configuration. 12) Documented integration patterns for Sportradar UOF, Genius LiveData, OPTA, IMG Arena, TxODDS Fusion odds feeds and for the GeoComply / Sumsub / Jumio compliance webhooks. 13) Cold-start strategy and WAL replay time benchmarks on tens of GB of hot state — a node restart during Super Bowl would be a regulator-reportable outage. 14) Published benchmark of strict-monetary path under 20:1 read:write load with 60-feature batch_get to validate trader-dashboard latency. 15) Worked example of distance primitive for CLV (price-taken vs closing-price distribution distance) and geo-VPN (consecutive geo_state distance) to make the differentiator concrete.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. Sportsbook risk genuinely needs an event-driven trigger primitive: 'when (event_id, market_id, selection_id).net_position crosses liability_cap, suspend market and notify trading'; 'when (account_id).stake_24h crosses state-mandated RG threshold, force cool-off prompt'; 'when (account_id).clv_30d_rank crosses 95th percentile, drop stake_factor bracket'; 'when (market_id, 60s).coordinated_sharp_inflow crosses N, freeze market for trader review'; 'when (account_id).deposit_30d crosses USD 10k without play, fire AML SAR review'; 'when (device_fp).distinct_account_24h crosses N, freeze accounts for collusion review'. Polling 30+ features per wager / score event just to threshold them is workable on the bet-acceptance path because the read is already happening, but is wasteful on the asynchronous AML / RG / integrity-monitoring / trader-alert paths. Triggers + auth + multi-tenancy + strict-monetary semantics are the four most-cited gaps for this domain.
